summary.headline: APL Apollo Q4 FY26: EBITDA per ton above INR5,500 on lower volumes, while management holds FY27 guidance of 15-20% volume and 20-25% EBITDA growth.
summary.overview: Management said Q4 FY26 volume rose 9% YoY and EBITDA per ton ran above INR5,500, with FY26 ROCE at 37% and free cash flow of INR13 billion. Volumes softened from late February after the Middle East crisis, due to steel and gas shortages, labour shortages and channel destocking, and April was slow at about 2.5 lakh tons. Management prioritised margin over volume and said full-year absolute EBITDA targets are unchanged. Net cash rose to about INR1,510 crore by end-March, aided by inventory reduction and better creditor terms.

financial_highlights.value: Above INR5,500/ton (Q4); Devarshi Jani cited INR5,525/ton
financial_highlights.change: Above the INR5,300-5,500 guided in Q3 call
From about INR550 crore at end-December 2025

financial_highlights.value: About INR350 crore cash flow generation in Q4
Down about INR250 crore from 31 Dec to 31 Mar

financial_highlights.change: Due to higher outward freight and branding spend

segments.name: Housing (application mix)
segments.commentary: Housing was 64% of mix, commercial buildings 23% and infrastructure 13%; management expects 2-3% mix shift to infra if government spending picks up.

segments.name: General products / Apollo brand
segments.commentary: General segment EBITDA per ton rose to INR3,500+ from about INR2,000, driven by the brand premium and a price hike of about INR1,500/ton taken in January 2025.

segments.name: Galvanised and coated products
segments.commentary: Margins improved on steel shortage; these lines were hit by temporary shutdowns of about 10-15 days in March from LPG/gas shortage and now run at 80-90% of capacity.

segments.name: Patra (low-margin channel)
segments.commentary: Volume share cut to below 30% of total and being reduced further to protect margins.

segments.name: SG Premium
segments.commentary: Accounted for 8-9% of total volume in Q4.

segments.name: Dubai operations
segments.commentary: Running at about 40% utilisation due to the Middle East crisis; volumes low but margins better per management.

guidance_outlook: FY27 guidance unchanged: volume growth 15-20%, EBITDA growth 20-25%, PAT growth 25-30%; management said 20% volume is difficult and the low end is 15%.
Absolute FY26 EBITDA target to be protected; management is not reducing guidance.

Monthly volume outlook: April about 2.5 lakh tons; May about 3 lakh tons; June about 3.5 lakh tons; FY27 volume could reach about 8.75 lakh tons per quarter-equivalent run-rate, against 7.92 lakh tons last year (as stated).
Sustainable EBITDA per ton of INR5,000-5,500 on a long-term basis; INR6,000+ possible currently but not assured.
Capex around INR500-600 crore per year; about INR1,400-1,500 crore pending for 8 million tonne capacity, to be completed in 2-2.5 years.
Once residual net liabilities of about INR500 crore are repaid in Q1-Q2, surplus cash may go to higher dividend or buyback; management said yes to a good dividend this year.
capex_capacity: Long-term target of 8 million tonne capacity by FY28 stated as on track.
Two new plants planned in East India; capacity to come on stream in next one to two years.
New Malur 2 plant in Bangalore for lighter structures in South India, to be built over the next two years.
Capex fully funded from internal cash flows.
Domestic plants run at 80-85% utilisation due to fear of fuel shortage; 15-20% upside if crisis fully ends (Dubai at about 40%).
demand_pricing: Volume hard to predict month to month; April slow and early May similar; construction sites halted by labour shortage from heat and elections.
Channel destocking under way amid fear of steel price correction; management said it cannot yet say whether this is destocking or demand slowdown.
HR coil prices rose about INR3,000/ton from April to May; this pass-through is reflected in realisation and cost.
Price increase of about INR4,500/ton on 1 April; inventory is largely at old rates, so inventory gain is minimal under monthly steel price revisions.
Market share gains expected from disruption hurting smaller players; management says strong players benefit more if disruption exceeds four months.

qa_highlights.question: Is the drop in volumes destocking or real demand weakness, and are guidance changes planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Gupta said it is too early to separate destocking from demand slowdown; yearly volume and profitability targets are intact, with focus on margin over volume.

qa_highlights.question: Can EBITDA per ton of INR5,500 be sustained given Patra pressure and Dubai weakness?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited market leadership, product innovation and steel shortage; INR5,000-5,500 is a two-year track record, INR6,000+ is uncertain.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FY27 capex and capital allocation plan?
qa_highlights.answer: Capex around INR500-600 crore per year; INR1,400-1,500 crore pending for 8 million tons, completed in 2-2.5 years. After about INR500 crore of liabilities are cleared, cash may go to dividend or buyback.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the EBITDA per ton gap versus value-added mix falling to 25% in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Anubhav Gupta said the general-segment spread rose to INR3,500+/ton from about INR2,000 on the brand premium and the January 2025 price hike, plus cost rationalisation.

qa_highlights.question: Has the company gained share in the disruption and how will it use its balance sheet?
qa_highlights.answer: Market share rose to 65% in FY26 from 55%; capex is self-funded, with two East India plants, Malur 2 and more SKU and branding spend.

qa_highlights.question: Is the April/May volume outlook and the gas-supply backup plan reflected in guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: April 2.5 lakh tons; May about 3 lakh tons; June about 3.5 lakh tons. March LPG disruption lasted 10-15 days; plants moved to alternate fuels and run at about 90%, and guidance factors this in.

risks_watch: Fuel and gas supply shortages could return; plants run at 80-90% due to fear of a repeat.
Steel price volatility and possible raw material shortage, with a risk of inventory losses if prices fall sharply.
Patra channel and smaller-player competition on price; Dubai utilisation at about 40%.
Volume recovery in May-June must hit about 3-3.5 lakh tons per month to support FY27 guidance.
Management said the 15% volume floor depends on the crisis not worsening; a fuel shortage affecting vehicles would prompt a plan review.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, brand and balance sheet, but cautious and evasive on near-term volumes; management declined quarterly or monthly guidance and repeatedly said the situation is hard to predict.
key_quotes: So, our focus right now is to protect our profitability and margins when we know that volume prediction becomes challenging in this environment
Volume, we are not focusing on our volume. We are focusing on our margin.
The capex is fully funded from internal cash flows.
So yes, I mean, if war had not started, we would have met our guidance which we had given in the quarter three.

New Malur 2 plant in Bangalore for lighter structures in South India

growth.why: FY27 guidance held at 15-20% volume (management calls 20% difficult, low end 15%) and 20-25% EBITDA growth, backed by a partly-funded 8 MT capacity build (INR1,400-1,500 crore pending, 2-2.5 years) and market share gains, but April volume was slow at ~2.5 lakh t and the brief gives no quantified order book.
